item.research_question: How can the structural tunability of high-entropy materials (HEMs), specifically the antisite disordering and lattice distortion, be leveraged to optimize catalytic performance and energy storage capabilities compared to traditional alloys or compounds?
item.material_system: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) such as PtPdRhRuCe, CoMoFeNiCu, AlNiCoFeX; High-entropy oxides (HEOs) such as (MgCoNiCuZn)Ox, (CoCuMgNiZn)Ox, Li-containing entropy-stabilized oxyfluorides; High-entropy metallic glasses (HEMGs); High-entropy borides (HEBs), carbides (HECs), sulfides (HESs), and nitrides (HENs)
item.processing_route: Synthesis methods include carbothermal shock (CTS) with thermal shock at ~2,000 K within 55 ms; fast-moving bed pyrolysis (FMBP) heating to ~923 K within 5 s; ultrasonication-assisted wet-chemistry with local temperatures up to ~5,000°C; electrodeposition confining precursors to water nanodroplets within 100 ms; solid-state sintering; solvothermal synthesis; and mechanochemical methods
item.test_conditions: Catalysis tested at temperatures up to 1500 K and reaction temperatures of 305 °C or 155 °C for CO oxidation; electrocatalysis performed at ~80 °C in acidic and basic electrolytes; battery cycling at rates up to 2000 mA/g; supercapacitor testing in 1 m KOH solution at 100 mV/s scan rate
key_findings: PtPdRhRuCe NPs achieved ~100% conversion and >99% nitrogen oxide selectivity for ammonia oxidation with no activity degradation.
Quinary CoMoFeNiCu NPs on carbon nanofiber showed a more than 20 times improvement in NH3 conversion rate versus Ru catalysts.
Co0.2Ni0.2Cu0.2Mg0.2Zn0.2O HEO achieved 98% conversion of benzyl alcohol in only 2 h under solvent-free aerobic oxidation.
Ni20Fe20Mo10Co35Cr15 HEA catalyst exhibited an overpotential of 107 mV in acidic solutions, comparable to Pt sheet.
Nanoporous AlCuNiPtMn exhibited a half-wave potential of 0.945 V in acidic media, representing a ~16-fold mass activity of Pt/C for ORR.
AuAgPtPdCu HEA catalyst achieved a faradaic efficiency of about 100% toward gaseous products at -0.3 V for CO2 reduction.
Rock-salt (Co0.2Cu0.2Mg0.2Ni0.2Zn0.2)O anode delivered an initial capacity of 446 mAh/g and 256 mAh/g after 100 cycles in a full cell.
Nanoporous AlCoCrFeNi HEA exhibited a high volumetric capacitance of 700 F/cm3 and excellent cycling stability of over 3,000 cycles.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute enhanced performance to the 'high-entropy effect', 'lattice distortion effect', 'sluggish diffusion effect', and 'cocktail effect', which stabilize single-phase solid solutions and create diverse local electronic structures and adsorption energies. The large number of atomic sites allows tuning of surface electronic structures and adsorption energies, while the uniform configuration leads to severe lattice distortion that increases the activation barrier of diffusion, improving kinetic stability.
item.limitations: The fundamental correlations between compositions and phases (e.g., phase diagrams) are not clear; the surface structures of HEMs may not be preserved at working conditions; productivity of HEA NPs via CTS is very low; the actual contribution of entropy versus enthalpy to Gibbs free energy is difficult to determine; and the surface structure of HEMs is more complicated than current catalysts.
item.future_work: Future work includes enhancing productivity for industrial applications, developing theoretical investigations using DFT and machine learning to design proper HEMs, achieving precise structural control of size, shape, and composition, developing 3D characterization techniques like electron tomography and APT, and exploring new types of HEMs with more than five elements.
quotes: Precursor of metal salt mixtures was thermally shocked at ~ 2,000 K within 55 ms (as shown in Figure 2A), alloying up to eight dissimilar elements into single-phase solid-solution NPs

The local temperature of the ultrasonication cavities is supposed to exceed extremely high temperature up to ∼ 5,000°C, directly accelerating the metallic ions reduction to form entropy-maximized state
The enhanced catalytic selectivity is suggested due to the highly atomically homogeneous nature of the solid-solution NPs, compared with the lower activity of the phase separated heterostructures
